notes:
# A shared screen is recorded, not a black rectangle {camcorder}
Zoom draws no meeting window while somebody presents, so a recording bound
to that window carried stretches of black -- Zoom, then a share, then Zoom
again, with the share missing from the file. It was tested by whether the
window still had a NAME, and a share leaves none: the reading came back a
confident "not in a meeting" while the same call was still going. Now the
capture asks whether the window it is bound to is still being DRAWN, and
whether this Mac's own share furniture is up, and follows the screen for as
long as the share lasts. The same wrong reading had two other costs: the
offer to record never appeared for anybody presenting, and because an
unnamed window was taken for a webinar, and a webinar is one-way, a
recording of your own presentation could come back with your voice left
out.

# Silence a meeting while it carries on recording {speaker}
A webinar you want recorded but do not want to sit through: turn Zoom's
sound off on this Mac and watch something else, and the recording and the
transcript carry on with every word. Only Zoom goes quiet -- everything
else on the Mac still plays -- and the meeting can still hear you. It needs
no audio driver installed: nothing to set up, and nothing left behind
afterwards. The switch is on the recording card, and the silence belongs to
the run, so the sound comes back by itself when the recording ends.

# The recording notice no longer changes your settings {shield}
"Send recording notice in chat" said this meeting and meant every meeting.
One press wrote the standing setting -- and switched Zoom's chat panel on
for good with it -- so every later meeting announced itself; and because a
Mac that announces everything has nothing left to be asked, the consent
panel never appeared again. The button now answers for the meeting in front
of you and nothing else. The standing answer is still there, as the switch
under Settings > Automation, where turning something on for good belongs.

# A licence handed back takes the quality with it {danger}
Recordings were always made at the trial's 720p whatever the store said --
that part was right. What was wrong is what the page showed: with a higher
preset still saved, none of the three cards read as chosen and the advanced
numbers behind them still said 1080p. The setting is brought down and saved
when the licence goes, so what the page says is what the recording will be.

# One click on the offer over Zoom {mic}
Every button on the panel that asks whether to record a meeting you joined
yourself needed pressing twice from another app: macOS spends the first
click on bringing an app forward, and that panel is only ever shown while
RecordLah is behind. It takes the first click now -- the two buttons, the
two tick boxes, and the close.

# While this is recording, two switches instead of two buttons {gear}
A button says what will happen; a switch says how things are. "Include my
voice" and the sound are switches now, showing the state rather than
offering the opposite of it -- and the sentence that said the same thing
again in words above them is gone. The sound one is called "Zoom sound on
this Mac" rather than "Mute meeting": in Zoom, Mute is your microphone, so
the familiar word was the confusing one.

# The elapsed clock stood still, then jumped {clock}
The time on the recording card showed 0:00 until the live transcript
started and then jumped to the real figure -- and with transcription off it
never moved at all. It was only ever advanced from inside the transcript's
own refresh. It starts at the truth and ticks every second now, whatever
else is switched on.

# The settings controls read as controls {sliders}
The box you type a number into was AppKit's own, which all but disappears
in light mode -- the one field on the page you could type a number into was
the one that did not look like a field. The menus were 24 points tall
against everything else's 30, and could not be made taller: a pop-up paints
its bezel at that size whatever room it is given. Both are the app's own
boxes now, at one height with the buttons beside them.

# A background check could make the window misbehave {danger}
The window runs sixteen small checks every two seconds. One of them
raising took the other fifteen with it and put an error out of the run loop
every two seconds, and a window whose beat is throwing stops behaving like
a window -- it was reported as an app that would not go behind. One
failure is now logged with what it was and skipped.

---

Everything else in this release:

- Turning your voice off part-way through a recording could end the run.
  The flag was read before it was declared, so the recorder stopped with
  an error a few seconds in -- the file was on disk, two seconds long,
  with nothing in the app pointing at it.
- The transcript names who said each line, by the name they use in Zoom,
  rather than only You or the meeting.
- Your own voice is no longer mistaken for the meeting's. The two labels
  fought over the same line, and every line you spoke alone could arrive
  marked as both of you: your microphone hears the meeting through your
  speakers, so the two readings are never independent.
- The live transcript is rebuilt to the design you asked for, with a
  waveform that moves while it listens rather than a badge that claims it
  is listening.
- Transcription no longer makes the Mac feel slow. It was starting more
  work than the machine could finish and starving the capture with it;
  the load fell from 86% to 16% of one core.
- The window could not be resized while a recording ran, and the reason
  was the offer to add your voice: a button that pins an exact width, put
  where the card's own width came from.
- Deleting a recording takes its folder with it, and the folder that held
  it if nothing is left in there. A folder with anything in it that the
  app did not put there is left exactly as it is.
- The transcriber opened a file for its own errors on every run and
  nothing ever wrote to one -- 54 empty files, each holding a folder open
  that would otherwise have been tidied away. It goes at the end of a run
  unless something was actually written to it.
- Empty recording folders left by earlier versions are swept up once a
  launch. 61 of them went on the first run.
- Storage reports the figure macOS itself shows. It read the raw one,
  which leaves out the space the system will reclaim when it needs to --
  4GB out of 31 on the Mac this was found on, and it read as the app
  being wrong about the disk.
- The note under a switch no longer says which way the switch is: it said
  "you are not hearing the meeting" over a control that was on, because
  nothing rebuilds the card when the sound is given back.
- Zoom sound and your voice can be changed while a recording runs, and the
  card says what is already recorded stays as it is.
- The capture note on Settings > Recording lost the half that explained
  where the Display control went, and the hairline that sat under its own
  border.
- The three switches on the recording card line up with each other.
- Installing a local build can no longer replace the app underneath a copy
  that is still running, which left it reading a file that had changed on
  disk and throwing every two seconds.
- Which folder a meeting is in is on its page now, beside the time zone
  and the link. It was the one fact there you had to open the edit form to
  read.
- Dragging a meeting onto the folders while they are folded away opens
  them. It was meant to already: it waited for the drag to MOVE again
  before noticing how long it had been there, so holding still over the
  header -- which is what waiting for something to open looks like -- did
  nothing at all.
- The log says which of the app's five programs started -- the window, the
  background helper, a recorder, the schedule, the transcriber -- and when
  the window came forward or went behind.
